narrationTexts: I'll dig into the log file.
finalText:
## What happened

**Root cause: Redis went away and never came back. Everything else is downstream of that.**

One caveat first — the log covers **2026-07-04 02:00–02:31 UTC**, not last night. Either this is an old file or the shipped log is stale; worth confirming you're looking at the right rotation before you act on it.

### Timeline

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00–02:14:03 | Fully healthy. 200s across `/users`, `/orders`, `/health`; cache hit ratio 0.90–0.98 |
| **02:14:07.113** | `ERROR [api] redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379` — **the trigger** (logs/app.log:182) |
| 02:14:07.114 | App falls back to direct store reads — cache layer degraded (logs/app.log:183) |
| 02:14:08 | Cache miss storm begins (`orders:1000`+, cycling through ~200 hot keys) |
| 02:14:10 | First `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` |
| 02:14:12 → 02:31:26 | Queue depth climbs monotonically, ~3 per sample, **52 → 568** |
| 02:29:12 | Queue crosses its own stated max: **depth 502 (max 500)** — and keeps accepting (logs/app.log:647) |
| 02:31:44 | `ERROR [worker-2] JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)` (logs/app.log:717) |
| 02:31:45 | `FATAL [supervisor] worker-2 exited with code 134, restarting` |
| **02:31:52** | `FATAL [supervisor] api unresponsive, killing process group — service down` |

**Volume:** 188 ERROR, 348 WARN, 2 FATAL. 173 of the errors are the same store timeout; 13 are Redis reconnect failures.

### The failure chain

Redis refuses connections → cache bypassed → every request hits the primary store → store saturates → 5s timeouts → requests pile up in the in-process queue instead of being shed → backlog consumes heap → worker-2 OOMs (SIGABRT/134) → api goes unresponsive → supervisor kills the process group. **~17.5 minutes from Redis loss to total outage.**

### Three problems worth fixing

1. **Redis never recovered.** 13 reconnect attempts (0 through 12), all `ECONNREFUSED` to the same `10.0.0.12:6379`, spaced at a **flat ~80 seconds** — no backoff progression, and more importantly no jitter and no success. The host was down or the endpoint moved; the app just kept knocking. Check whether that IP is still valid (failover/re-IP?) and why nothing paged on the first ECONNREFUSED.

2. **The queue cap is decorative.** Logs say `max 500` but depth sailed past it to 568 with no shedding, no 503s, no circuit breaker. That cap is what should have kept the process alive in a degraded-but-serving state. This is what turned a cache outage into a full outage.

3. **No cache-miss protection.** The miss storm cycles the same ~200 `orders:*` keys repeatedly — a request coalescer / singleflight would have collapsed those into one store read per key instead of stampeding.

I can't check the implementation — the repo here is only `package.json` (`incident-service` 2.4.0, ioredis ^5.4.1) and the log; there's no `src/`. Point me at the source and I'll look at the reconnect config and queue admission logic.
